name: Caldero Patchwork Layered Tank
description:
A Shelf staple assembled from salvaged textile scraps — panels of faded corporate workwear fabric stitched alongside strips of what was once a West African kente-print garment, a section of silver-gray thermal lining, and a band of heavy denim along one shoulder. No two Caldero tanks are identical because there is no Caldero — it's a street name for the guy on the Tier 1 market stall at the corner of Caldero and 9th who sews these by hand from whatever comes in that week. The stitching is visible, sometimes doubled where the fabric was thin, and the whole thing has a raw hem at the bottom that curls slightly after washing.

Worn close to the body, it breathes better than it looks. Shelf kids wear these under everything, or alone in summer, and the layered construction means there's always a pocket sewn somewhere unexpected — inside the kente panel, under the denim patch. It's not fashionable in any conventional sense, but on the Shelf it reads as resourceful, and resourceful is respected.
what_it_says: You survive on the Shelf and you're not embarrassed about it. You've stopped pretending otherwise.
story_hooks: A particular Caldero tank stitched together from a dead man's jacket becomes recognizable to people who knew him — and someone wants it back.
The hidden inner pocket has a hand-sewn label that reads a date, a name, and nothing else.
A Tier 4 fashion scout photographs someone wearing one on the Shelf and tries to license the 'aesthetic' — the original maker has opinions about this.

physical_description.visual_profile: A patchwork sleeveless tank with visibly mismatched fabric panels creating a deliberately fragmented aesthetic. The silhouette is lean and close-fitting, emphasizing the body's natural lines. Reads as street-salvaged and hand-assembled rather than manufactured—the visual chaos is the point. On a wearer, it communicates resourcefulness and Shelf authenticity.
physical_description.fit: Slim, close to the body with minimal excess fabric. Cut to hug the torso without restriction, allowing for mobility and layering underneath. Slightly cropped in some iterations depending on panel arrangement.
physical_description.primary_material: Salvaged mixed textiles: faded corporate workwear cotton-blend, West African kente-print cotton, silver-gray thermal synthetic lining, heavy raw denim. Each panel sourced from end-of-life garments and scrap bins.
physical_description.texture: Visibly varied—smooth sections alternate with rougher denim weave, thermal panels show subtle quilting. Raw, hand-curled hem at the bottom. Heavy visible stitching, sometimes doubled or imperfect, adds tactile roughness. Fabrics show fading, minor fraying at seams.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary palette of muted tones: faded indigo and gray corporate fabric, deep kente-print ochre and burgundy stripes, silver-gray thermal accent, dark raw denim shoulder band. Worn, desaturated overall impression with pops of traditional West African color.
physical_description.closures: None. Pulls on over the head. Fit is integral to design.
distinctive_features: Visibly hand-stitched seams—raw, sometimes doubled or offset
Raw, curled hem at bottom edge
Unexpected interior pocket sewn into kente section
Heavy denim reinforcement along one shoulder
Silver-gray thermal lining patch (likely repurposed from insulation)
Seams show wear and washable deterioration
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 / Shelf sub-grade. Signals resourcefulness and street economy participation, not poverty but rejection of corpo supply chains.
physical_description.cultural_context: Shelf kid uniform. Worn by those who source from street markets, value repair culture over consumption, and exist outside formal tier hierarchies. Kente integration signals diasporic heritage normalization in GLMZ. Reads as authentic to those who navigate ungoverned zones.
physical_description.condition_typical: Deliberately worn-in and imperfect. Never pristine. Shows visible use—minor fraying, faded seams, slight curl to raw hem after multiple washes. Patched seams occasionally reinforced by wearer with mismatched thread. Weathered authenticity is the design intent.
